paper_metadata.title: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo Method with a Neural-Network Ansatz for Open Quantum Systems

summary: The paper introduces a classical variational Monte Carlo method using a Restricted Boltzmann Machine density‑matrix ansatz to approximate the non‑equilibrium steady state of open quantum systems. It demonstrates the approach on dissipative XYZ spin models on 2×2 and 3×3 lattices, showing convergence to exact results as the RBM hidden-node densities increase (e.g., α = β up to 3) and identifying a dissipative phase transition around Jy/γ ≈ 1.04.

experiments.description: Variational Monte Carlo simulation of the non-equilibrium steady state of a dissipative 2D XYZ spin model using a neural-network density-matrix ansatz (RBM) and stochastic reconfiguration.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo with neural-network density-matrix ansatz (RBM) and stochastic reconfiguration
algorithm.convergence_criteria: iterate SR until observables and ⟨⟨Lχ⟩⟩ converge; no explicit stopping threshold reported

hyperparameters.alpha: M/N, hidden-node density for wave-function RBM
hyperparameters.beta: L/N, hidden-node density for mixture RBM
hyperparameters.NMH: number of Metropolis-Hastings steps set to roughly Np

algorithm.parameter_initialization: parameters initialized to small random values

problem_formulation.encoding_details: spin-1/2 lattice basis with σ_i, η_i ∈ {−1,1}; density matrix sampled in computational basis
problem_formulation.objective_function: find steady state ρ_ss satisfying L(ρ_ss)=0 by maximizing the real part of the Liouvillian expectation value / minimizing ⟨⟨Lχ⟩⟩ toward zero
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: trace normalization implicit in normalized expectation values; positivity/self-adjointness enforced by density-matrix ansatz
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H = Σ_<i,j> (Jx σx_i σx_j + Jy σy_i σy_j + Jz σz_i σz_j) with local dissipation γ via Lindblad jump operators σ^-_k

problem_instance.description: Dissipative XYZ spin model on 2D periodic lattices; observables include magnetization and steady-state spin structure factor

dataset_specification.description: 2×2, 3×3, and 3×3 lattices studied; parameters varied across phase boundary

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: compare VMC observables against exact results; average observables over 100 parameter sets in asymptotic SR region

implementation_details.classical_solver: Metropolis-Hastings sampling; MINRES-QLP for linear system in SR
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute magnetization Mz and structure factor Sxx_ss(k) from optimized density matrix; compare to exact values

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: SR evolution of Re(⟨⟨Lχ⟩⟩) shown to oscillate early and converge asymptotically

implementation_details.framework: Python VMC code with CPU and GPU implementations using MVAPICH2 parallelization and MINRES-QLP linear solver

speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum speedup claim is made; the work reports a classical VMC method and compares against exact results on small lattices.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(Np^3 + Np Nc) for the VMC/SR evaluation as stated
